brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Separate compartments so small notions (bobbins, pins, buttons, needles) don't mix
A larger open space for bulkier items (thread spools, scissors, tape, scraps)
requirements.evidence: bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full, a full-depth bin with no dividers.

requirements.requirement: Closed so supplies stay tidy and dust-free and pins can't spill
requirements.evidence: Solid top covers on all three cells, plus caps on all 12 open side faces.
Joint bolts on all three shared walls (jointBolt:0#0,0#0, 0#0,0#5, 0#0,1#1). The loose-body warnings went away.
find_sockets offered no handle place on this 3-cell build, even after covers and caps were fitted, so none were added.
check_build: no issues, meshClash clear. 27 parts in total.

finish.summary: A small three-cell sewing organiser: three full bases in a triangle, bolted together, each with its own bin, a solid lid and closed sides. No rule errors and the mesh check is clear. Handles weren't offered anywhere on this layout, so the lids have none.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
